'''''Impatiens balfourii''''' is a species of the genus ''[[Impatiens]]'' known by the common names '''Balfour's touch-me-not''', '''Kashmir balsam''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''poor man's orchid'''. It belongs to the family [[Balsaminaceae]].

==Etymology==
The Latin name ''Impatiens'' means "impatient" or "intolerant" and refers to the [[explosive dehiscence]] of the fruits, which burst at the slightest touch as a means of scattering the seeds. The Latin species epithet ''balfourii'' honors the Scottish botanist [[Isaac Bayley Balfour]] (1853-1922).<ref>Hooker, J.D. (1903) in ''Curtis's Botanical Magazine''. vol. 129 tab. 7878</ref>

==Description==
This is an [[Annual plant|annual]] [[herb]] growing {{convert|15|-|120|cm}} in height. Its stem is glabrous, reddish, lined and very branched. It has alternately arranged, oval to lance-shaped, toothed, stalked leaves up to {{convert|4|cm}} long. The [[inflorescence]] is a [[raceme]] generally bearing 4 to 8 flowers. Each flower is about {{convert|2|cm}} long, with one of its white [[sepal]]s forming a long, thin spur, and two of its yellow-dotted lavender or pink petals extending from the mouth.

==Reproduction==
The flowers are [[Plant reproductive morphology|hermaphrodite]], or perfect, and are [[Entomophily|pollinated by insects]], or, in the Americas, by [[hummingbird]]s. The flowering period extends from July through September. The fruits are glabrous [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]]s about {{convert|20|mm}} long and the seeds are [[seed dispersal|dispersed]] when the fruits burst, launching them up to {{convert|6|m}} away.

==Distribution==
It is native to the [[Himalayas]], particularly [[Kashmir]] and surrounding areas, where it grows in mountains of 5,000 to 6,000 feet.<ref name=pp>Peirce, P. & D. Goldberg. [https://books.google.com/books?id=b6VKo5W9KmYC&dq=impatiens+balfourii&pg=PA75 ''Wildly Successful Plants: Northern California'']. Sasquatch Books. 2004. 75-77.</ref> It was brought back to England and many other European countries as a [[ornamental plant|garden plant]], and then it became popular in the [[San Francisco Bay Area]] and other parts of the United States.<ref name=pp/> It can now be found growing wild as a garden escapee in [[Europe]], on the US Pacific Coast, and in [[Wisconsin]],<ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=IMBA2 USDA Plants Profile]</ref> where it is a restricted species because of its invasiveness.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Balfour's touch-me-not {{!}} Wisconsin DNR|url=https://dnr.wisconsin.gov/topic/Invasives/fact/BalfoursTouch-me-not.html|access-date=2021-08-14|website=dnr.wisconsin.gov}}</ref>

==Habitat==
In the wild the plant occurs along the banks of rivers, on roadsides, and in wastelands. It thrives in cool and moist areas, at an altitude of {{convert|100|-|600|m}} above sea level.
